answer: Continuous physical-presence beaconing. Each agent holds a hardware key that signs a rolling cipher challenge tied to a witnessed location pulse; the network only accepts identities whose pulses trace one continuous body over time. A haven of idle keys fails because presence cannot be replayed. Reaching the reputation zenith requires years of unbroken pulses. An attacker pays one human supervisor per concurrent identity, plus hardware and travel, making mass duplication cost-prohibitive.
